name: Labrador Retriever
lore: The world's most popular dog breed for over 30 years. Originally bred to help fishermen haul nets and catch fish in icy waters.
dietNotes: Prone to obesity; measure meals carefully and limit treats. Needs high-quality protein with controlled fat content.

name: German Shepherd
lore: Renowned for intelligence and versatility. Serves as police dogs, guide dogs, and search-and-rescue heroes worldwide.
dietNotes: Feed a high-protein diet formulated for large active breeds. Split meals into two servings to help prevent bloat.

name: Golden Retriever
lore: Bred by Lord Tweedmouth in the Scottish Highlands. Their gentle mouth can carry a raw egg without cracking it.
dietNotes: Needs a balanced diet with omega fatty acids for coat health. Monitor portions closely as they tend to overeat.

name: French Bulldog
lore: Originally bred as miniature Bulldogs in England, they became wildly popular with Parisian lace workers in the 1800s.
dietNotes: Feed a high-quality diet for small breeds. Prone to food allergies; limited-ingredient diets may help. Avoid overfeeding due to low exercise tolerance.

name: Bulldog
lore: Once bred for bull-baiting, today's Bulldog is a gentle couch potato. They're the mascot of the US Marine Corps.
dietNotes: Very prone to obesity; strict portion control is essential. Feed a moderate-calorie diet and keep facial wrinkles clean after meals.

name: Poodle
lore: One of the most intelligent breeds. Their fancy haircuts originally served a practical purpose — keeping joints warm while swimming.
dietNotes: Needs high-quality protein to support an active lifestyle. Regular meals with omega fatty acids help maintain their curly coat.

name: Beagle
lore: Their incredible nose has 220 million scent receptors. Used by USDA at airports to sniff out contraband food.
dietNotes: Notorious food thieves; secure all food and measure meals carefully. Prone to obesity if allowed free-feeding.

name: Rottweiler
lore: Descended from Roman drover dogs. Butchers in Rottweil used them to pull carts of meat to market.
dietNotes: Requires a large-breed formula with joint-supporting nutrients. Feed two meals daily to reduce bloat risk; avoid exercise right after eating.

name: Yorkshire Terrier
lore: Originally bred to catch rats in clothing mills. Despite tiny size, they have the heart of a terrier.
dietNotes: Small stomachs need nutrient-dense food in small, frequent meals. Dental-friendly kibble helps prevent tooth problems common in the breed.

name: Dachshund
lore: The 'sausage dog' was bred to hunt badgers underground. Their name literally means 'badger dog' in German.
dietNotes: Weight management is critical to protect their long spine. Feed measured portions and avoid letting them jump on/off furniture.

name: Boxer
lore: Named for their habit of playing by standing on hind legs and 'boxing' with their front paws. Eternal puppies at heart.
dietNotes: Feed high-quality, grain-inclusive diet with good protein sources. Two meals daily to reduce bloat risk. Avoid foods with excessive fillers.

name: Siberian Husky
lore: The Chukchi people bred them for endurance sled pulling. In 1925, Huskies ran a life-saving serum relay 674 miles to Nome, Alaska.
dietNotes: Surprisingly efficient eaters that need less food than their size suggests. High-protein diet with fish-based omega oils for coat health.

name: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
lore: Named after King Charles II, who was so devoted to them that he decreed they be allowed in any public place, including Parliament.
dietNotes: Heart-healthy diet with omega-3 fatty acids is beneficial. Monitor weight as they can easily become overweight with their love of treats.

name: Doberman Pinscher
lore: Created by tax collector Louis Dobermann who wanted a loyal guard dog. One of the smartest and most trainable breeds.
dietNotes: Feed a high-protein, heart-healthy diet with taurine supplementation. Active dogs need calorie-dense food split into two daily meals.

name: Great Dane
lore: Despite their name, they're German, not Danish. The tallest dog ever recorded was a Great Dane named Zeus at 44 inches.
dietNotes: Must use large-breed puppy food for slow, steady growth. Feed 2-3 small meals daily from an elevated bowl to reduce bloat risk.

name: Australian Shepherd
lore: Despite the name, they were developed in the American West. Rodeo performers made them famous with incredible trick routines.
dietNotes: High-energy dogs need calorie-dense food with quality protein. Adjust portions based on activity level; working dogs need significantly more.

name: Miniature Schnauzer
lore: Bred down from Standard Schnauzers crossed with Poodles. Their distinctive beard and eyebrows give them a wise, old-man look.
dietNotes: Prone to pancreatitis; feed a low-fat, high-quality diet. Avoid fatty table scraps entirely. Regular feeding schedule is important.

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
lore: Queen Elizabeth II owned over 30 Corgis during her lifetime. Welsh legend says fairies rode them into battle.
dietNotes: Very prone to obesity; strict portion control is essential. Feed a balanced diet and resist their expert begging skills.

name: Shih Tzu
lore: Bred as palace pets for Chinese emperors. Their name means 'lion dog' and they were treasured as living hot water bottles.
dietNotes: Small-breed formula with small kibble size for their flat face. Keep hair around the face trimmed to avoid food contamination.

name: Cocker Spaniel
lore: Named for their skill hunting woodcock. The inspiration for Lady in Disney's 'Lady and the Tramp.'
dietNotes: Feed a balanced diet with omega fatty acids for their luxurious coat. Keep ears clean especially after eating from bowls to prevent infections.

name: Pomeranian
lore: Descended from large sled-pulling Spitz dogs. Queen Victoria's tiny Pomeranian sparked a craze for breeding them smaller.
dietNotes: Tiny dogs need nutrient-dense, small-kibble food. Prone to low blood sugar; feed small meals 3 times daily rather than twice.

name: Chihuahua
lore: The world's smallest dog breed, named after the Mexican state. Ancient Aztecs believed they guided souls through the underworld.
dietNotes: Very small stomachs require nutrient-dense food in tiny portions. Prone to hypoglycemia; provide small frequent meals throughout the day.

name: Border Collie
lore: Widely considered the most intelligent dog breed. Chaser, a Border Collie, learned the names of over 1,000 objects.
dietNotes: Extremely active dogs need high-calorie, protein-rich food. Working dogs may need 25-30% more calories than typical recommendations.

name: Pug
lore: Ancient Chinese emperors prized Pugs so much they were guarded by soldiers. Their wrinkles were bred to form the Chinese character for 'prince.'
dietNotes: Highly prone to obesity; strictly measure all food and treats. Use a flat bowl or slow feeder to prevent gulping air while eating.

name: Maltese
lore: One of the oldest toy breeds, dating back over 2,000 years. Ancient Greeks built tombs for their beloved Maltese.
dietNotes: Small-breed formula with easily digestible proteins. Tear staining can be diet-related; avoid foods with artificial dyes and excess iron.

name: Bernese Mountain Dog
lore: Swiss farm dogs that pulled milk carts through Alpine villages. One of four Swiss mountain dog breeds, and the only one with long hair.
dietNotes: Large-breed formula with joint-supporting glucosamine. Prone to bloat; feed 2-3 smaller meals and avoid vigorous exercise after eating.

name: Weimaraner
lore: The 'Gray Ghost' was bred for hunting large game like boar and deer. Their striking silver-gray coat and amber eyes are unmistakable.
dietNotes: High-energy breed needs calorie-dense food with quality animal proteins. Feed two meals daily and use a slow feeder to reduce bloat risk.

name: Rhodesian Ridgeback
lore: Originally bred to track lions in Africa. The distinctive ridge on their back is formed by hair growing in the opposite direction.
dietNotes: Athletic breed needs high-protein diet with moderate fat. Feed twice daily; they can be food-possessive, so teach good mealtime manners early.

name: Akita
lore: The legendary Hachiko waited for his deceased owner at a Tokyo train station every day for nearly 10 years. A national treasure of Japan.
dietNotes: Feed a high-quality large-breed formula. Some Akitas are sensitive to certain proteins; monitor for food allergies. Two meals daily to prevent bloat.

name: Dalmatian
lore: Born pure white, they develop their spots as they grow. Historically ran alongside horse-drawn fire carriages to guard the equipment.
dietNotes: Unique purine metabolism requires a low-purine diet. Avoid organ meats, sardines, and high-purine foods. Ensure plenty of fresh water.

name: Whippet
lore: Can reach 35 mph in seconds, making them the fastest accelerating dog breed. Known as the 'poor man's racehorse.'
dietNotes: Lean sighthound needs moderate-calorie diet. Their thin frame means even a little extra weight is noticeable and harmful. Feed twice daily.

name: Irish Setter
lore: Their gorgeous mahogany coat made them show ring favorites. President Nixon's Irish Setter, King Timahoe, lived in the White House.
dietNotes: High-energy sporting dog needs protein-rich food. Prone to bloat; feed 2-3 smaller meals using a slow feeder. Avoid exercise after meals.

name: Samoyed
lore: The Samoyede people slept with these dogs for warmth in -60F temperatures. Their permanent smile prevents drooling that would form icicles.
dietNotes: Needs a balanced diet with good protein for their thick double coat. Originally thrived on fish and reindeer; fish-based diets work well.

name: Bull Terrier
lore: Bred from Bulldogs and terriers for dog fighting, now beloved clowns. General Patton's Bull Terrier, Willie, accompanied him through WWII.
dietNotes: Feed a balanced, protein-rich diet. Some are prone to skin allergies; a limited-ingredient diet can help identify triggers.

name: Basset Hound
lore: Their droopy ears sweep scent off the ground toward their nose. Second only to Bloodhounds in tracking ability.
dietNotes: Extremely prone to obesity; strict calorie control is critical. Their soulful begging eyes are deceiving; do not overfeed.

name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier
lore: Known as the 'nanny dog' in England for their gentle patience with children. Incredibly loyal and affectionate despite their tough appearance.
dietNotes: Muscular breed needs protein-rich diet. Active dogs with good appetites; measure meals to maintain lean muscle without excess weight.

name: Shetland Sheepdog
lore: Miniature Collies from the Shetland Islands. They're so eager to please that they consistently rank among the top breeds in obedience competitions.
dietNotes: Active herding breed needs quality protein and omega fatty acids for their abundant coat. MDR1 gene means some drugs interact with diet.

name: Vizsla
lore: Hungary's national dog, called the 'Velcro Vizsla' for their need to be constantly touching their owner. Ancient Magyar warriors hunted with them.
dietNotes: Extremely active breed needs high-calorie, protein-rich food. Lean athletes that burn calories fast; adjust portions to activity level.

name: Bichon Frise
lore: Renaissance royalty adored them. After the French Revolution, they survived by performing tricks as circus dogs.
dietNotes: Feed a high-quality small-breed formula. Prone to allergies; grain-free or limited-ingredient diets may benefit sensitive individuals.

name: Airedale Terrier
lore: The 'King of Terriers' — largest of all terrier breeds. Served as messenger dogs and sentries in both World Wars.
dietNotes: Active large terrier needs protein-rich food. Prone to skin issues; omega fatty acids and high-quality proteins support skin and coat health.

name: Belgian Malinois
lore: The elite military working dog. Cairo, a Malinois, was part of the SEAL Team Six raid on Osama bin Laden.
dietNotes: Extremely high-energy working dog needs calorie-dense, protein-rich food. Working Malinois may need 30-40% more calories than pet dogs.

name: Bloodhound
lore: Can follow a scent trail over 300 hours old. Their trailing evidence is admissible in court — the only breed with this distinction.
dietNotes: Very bloat-prone; feed 2-3 small meals daily from an elevated dish. Wipe face and ears after eating to prevent skin fold infections.

name: English Springer Spaniel
lore: Named for their ability to 'spring' game from hiding. They can work tirelessly in the field all day and cuddle all evening.
dietNotes: Active sporting dog needs balanced nutrition with good protein. Keep ears clean after meals; floppy ears trap moisture and food debris.

name: Cane Corso
lore: Ancient Roman war dog descended from the Molossus. Their name means 'guardian dog' in Latin. Nearly went extinct in the 1970s.
dietNotes: Large, muscular breed needs high-protein, large-breed formula. Feed 2-3 meals daily to prevent bloat. Use slow feeders for fast eaters.

name: Newfoundland
lore: Born to swim — they have webbed feet and a water-resistant coat. A Newfoundland is credited with saving Napoleon Bonaparte from drowning.
dietNotes: Giant breed needs large-breed formula with controlled calcium for joint health. Prone to bloat; feed multiple smaller meals rather than one large one.

name: Papillon
lore: Named for their butterfly-like ears ('papillon' is French for butterfly). Marie Antoinette reportedly walked to the guillotine carrying her Papillon.
dietNotes: Small-breed formula with nutrient-dense ingredients. Active little dogs with fast metabolisms; ensure consistent feeding schedule.

name: Saint Bernard
lore: Alpine rescue dogs that saved over 2,000 travelers in the Swiss Alps. Barry, the most famous, rescued over 40 people.
dietNotes: Giant breed needs controlled-calorie diet to prevent rapid growth. Feed 2-3 meals daily; avoid free-feeding. Joint supplements are beneficial.

name: Alaskan Malamute
lore: One of the oldest Arctic sled dogs, bred by the Inuit Mahlemut people. Can pull loads up to 3,000 pounds.
dietNotes: Working sled dogs are efficient eaters; they need less food than expected. High-protein, moderate-fat diet works best. Avoid overfeeding.

name: West Highland White Terrier
lore: Bred white so hunters wouldn't mistake them for foxes. Their confident strut and perky ears make them one of the most recognizable terriers.
dietNotes: Prone to skin allergies; a limited-ingredient or hypoallergenic diet can help. Avoid chicken-based foods if skin issues develop.

name: Jack Russell Terrier
lore: Named after Reverend John Russell, who bred them for fox hunting. Pound for pound, one of the most energetic dogs on Earth.
dietNotes: Extremely energetic small dog needs calorie-dense food. Despite small size, they burn enormous energy and need more food than you might expect.

name: Afghan Hound
lore: One of the oldest dog breeds, said to have been on Noah's Ark. Their flowing coat protected them in the harsh Afghan mountains.
dietNotes: Lean sighthound with fast metabolism. Feed a high-quality, protein-rich diet. Some benefit from elevated food bowls to protect their long necks.

name: Irish Wolfhound
lore: The tallest of all dog breeds. Ancient Irish laws only allowed kings and nobles to own them. They hunted wolves to extinction in Ireland.
dietNotes: Giant breed with short lifespan needs giant-breed formula. Feed 2-3 small meals daily to prevent bloat. Avoid heavy exercise around mealtimes.

name: Borzoi
lore: Russian aristocracy bred them for wolf hunting. Leo Tolstoy immortalized them in 'War and Peace.' Can reach speeds of 40 mph.
dietNotes: Deep-chested sighthound very prone to bloat. Feed 2-3 small meals daily and avoid exercise 1 hour before and after eating.

name: Komondor
lore: Their iconic corded coat makes them look like a giant mop, but it protects them from wolf bites while guarding sheep.
dietNotes: Large guardian breed needs high-quality, moderate-calorie food. Feed twice daily; prone to bloat so avoid exercise around meals.

name: Basenji
lore: The 'barkless dog' — they yodel instead of bark. Ancient Egyptians gave Basenjis as gifts to pharaohs. They groom themselves like cats.
dietNotes: Monitor for Fanconi syndrome symptoms that affect kidney function. Fresh water always available. High-quality protein diet in measured portions.

name: Xoloitzcuintli
lore: Over 3,000 years old, the ancient Aztec hairless dog. Named after the god Xolotl, who guided the dead. Considered national treasure of Mexico.
dietNotes: Hairless variety needs extra skin-supporting nutrients. Diet rich in omega fatty acids helps maintain healthy skin. Apply sunscreen before outdoor time.

name: Chinese Crested
lore: Chinese sailors kept them on ships to hunt rats. The hairless variety has silky hair on head, tail, and feet — looking like a tiny punk rocker.
dietNotes: Hairless variety has dental issues; soft food may be needed. Small frequent meals; prone to weight gain if overfed.

name: Saluki
lore: The 'Royal Dog of Egypt,' possibly the oldest domesticated breed. Mummified Salukis have been found in pharaohs' tombs.
dietNotes: Lean sighthound with low body fat; they naturally appear thin. Feed a high-quality, moderate-calorie diet. Sensitive to anesthesia.

name: Tibetan Mastiff
lore: Guardian of Himalayan monasteries. In 2014, a Tibetan Mastiff sold for $1.95 million in China, making it the most expensive dog ever sold.
dietNotes: Guardian breed that eats less than their size suggests. Feed a large-breed formula; they may self-regulate food intake seasonally.

name: Pharaoh Hound
lore: National dog of Malta. One of the few breeds that can blush — their nose and ears turn rosy when excited.
dietNotes: Athletic sighthound needs quality protein with moderate fat. Lean breed; avoid overfeeding but ensure enough calories for their active lifestyle.

name: Norwegian Lundehund
lore: Has six toes on each foot and can tip their head backward to touch their spine. Bred to hunt puffins on cliffsides.
dietNotes: Prone to serious intestinal issues (Lundehund syndrome). May need special easily digestible diet. Consult vet for breed-specific dietary needs.

name: Bedlington Terrier
lore: Looks like a lamb but hunts like a wolf. Originally bred by miners in Bedlington to catch rats and race for sport.
dietNotes: Prone to copper storage disease; avoid foods high in copper (organ meats, shellfish). Requires a specifically low-copper diet if affected.

name: Leonberger
lore: Created to resemble the lion on the city crest of Leonberg. Used as water rescue dogs thanks to their webbed feet and massive size.
dietNotes: Giant breed needs slow, controlled growth as a puppy. Feed large-breed formula in 2-3 meals daily. Joint supplements recommended.

name: Otterhound
lore: One of the rarest breeds — fewer than 800 exist worldwide. Their webbed feet and oily double coat made them perfect otter hunters.
dietNotes: Active hound needs good-quality food with balanced protein and fat. Can be messy eaters; their beard collects food and water.

name: Lagotto Romagnolo
lore: The world's only breed specifically bred for truffle hunting. Their curly, waterproof coat and exceptional nose make them truffle-finding machines.
dietNotes: Active working breed needs quality protein. Their curly coat benefits from omega fatty acids. Moderate portions to maintain a healthy weight.

name: Azawakh
lore: A Saharan sighthound from the Tuareg nomads. So lean that their bone structure is visible through their skin — built for desert heat.
dietNotes: Naturally lean sighthound; visible ribs are normal for the breed. Feed a high-quality protein diet; they may eat less in hot weather.

name: Bergamasco Sheepdog
lore: Their coat naturally forms into felt-like mats that protect against weather and predators. Once set, it never needs brushing.
dietNotes: Hardy breed with modest dietary needs. Feed a balanced large-breed diet. Once their coat 'sets' into mats, grooming needs are surprisingly low.

name: Thai Ridgeback
lore: One of only three ridgeback breeds. Isolated on Thai islands for centuries, they evolved independently and can even climb trees.
dietNotes: Active, primitive breed does well on high-protein diets. Not prone to obesity but should still have measured meals twice daily.

name: Peruvian Inca Orchid
lore: Ancient Inca hairless dog considered magical. The Incas believed their body heat could cure arthritis and respiratory ailments.
dietNotes: Hairless breed needs skin-nourishing diet rich in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids. Dental issues may require softer foods.

name: Mudi
lore: A rare Hungarian herding breed that can manage flocks of up to 500 sheep single-handedly. Also excels at hunting wild boar.
dietNotes: High-energy herding breed needs calorie-dense food. Active working dogs need more calories; adjust based on activity level.

name: Catalburun
lore: One of only three breeds with a split nose (double nose). Fewer than 200 exist outside Turkey. Exceptional pointer with incredible scent ability.
dietNotes: Active pointer needs high-quality protein diet. Feed twice daily; moderate portions appropriate for their medium build and activity level.

name: New Guinea Singing Dog
lore: A wild canid only recently studied, known for their haunting, harmonic howl. Can climb trees and bend their spine like a cat.
habitat: Hound Group | Origin: Papua New Guinea
dietNotes: Primitive breed does well on a high-protein diet. They are resourceful eaters in the wild; domestic feeding should mimic whole-prey nutrition.

name: Chinook
lore: New Hampshire's state dog, bred by explorer Arthur Walden. Nearly went extinct with only 11 dogs left in 1981. A true American original.
dietNotes: Working sled dog breed needs good-quality, protein-rich food. Moderate fat content; adjust calories to activity level.

name: Telomian
lore: One of the rarest breeds. Malaysian indigenous people bred them to climb ladders to enter raised houses. Can grasp objects with their paws.
dietNotes: Primitive breed thrives on high-protein diet. Small but active; feed measured meals twice daily with quality animal protein.

name: Carolina Dog
lore: America's own 'dingo' — feral dogs discovered in South Carolina's swamps. DNA suggests they crossed the Bering land bridge with ancient humans.
dietNotes: Hardy, primitive breed with few dietary issues. Benefits from high-protein, whole-ingredient foods. Moderate portions twice daily.

name: Kai Ken
lore: A natural monument of Japan. Their brindle coat earned them the nickname 'Tiger Dog.' So rare that even in Japan, few have seen one.
dietNotes: Japanese breed traditionally fed fish-based diets. Quality protein with omega fatty acids supports their brindle double coat.

name: Stabyhoun
lore: One of the five rarest breeds in the world. Only about 7,000 exist globally. A versatile Dutch farm dog that excels at everything.
dietNotes: Versatile sporting breed needs balanced nutrition with quality protein. Not prone to obesity but meals should still be measured.

name: Fila Brasileiro
lore: So loyal that a Brazilian proverb says 'faithful as a Fila.' Bred to track escaped slaves and jaguars. Banned in several countries.
dietNotes: Giant guardian breed needs large-breed formula with joint support. Prone to bloat; feed 2-3 smaller meals daily instead of one large meal.

name: Canaan Dog
lore: Descended from the pariah dogs of ancient Canaan. Used by the Israeli military as mine detectors and messengers.
dietNotes: Hardy desert breed with efficient metabolism. Quality protein diet in moderate portions; they tend to be easy keepers.

name: Kooikerhondje
lore: Dutch duck decoying dogs that lured ducks into traps by wagging their fluffy white-tipped tails. A Kooiker allegedly saved William of Orange's life.
dietNotes: Active sporting breed needs balanced nutrition. Not prone to overeating; feed measured meals with quality protein twice daily.

name: Japanese Chin
lore: Treasured by Japanese royalty for over a thousand years. These dainty lapdogs were gifts between noble houses and prized for their cat-like grace.
dietNotes: Toy breed needs small, nutrient-dense meals. Their flat face can make eating difficult; use shallow, wide bowls.

name: Pekingese
lore: Sacred dogs of the Chinese imperial palace. Commoners had to bow to them, and stealing one was punishable by death.
dietNotes: Flat-faced breed prone to overheating; avoid warm food. Small meals with quality protein; monitor weight closely as excess weight worsens breathing.

name: Blenheim Spaniel
lore: Named after Blenheim Palace where the Duke of Marlborough bred chestnut-and-white spaniels. A color variety of the King Charles Spaniel.
dietNotes: Heart-healthy diet with omega-3 fatty acids. Monitor portions as they gain weight easily. Small-breed formula works well.

name: Toy Terrier
lore: A miniature version of the Manchester Terrier, bred to hunt rats in Victorian England. Despite their tiny size, they have a bold terrier spirit.
dietNotes: Tiny breed needs small, frequent meals of nutrient-dense food. Dental-sized kibble helps maintain oral health.

name: Bluetick Coonhound
lore: Named for their distinctive blue-mottled coat. Bred in Louisiana to track raccoons, they have one of the most melodious baying voices of any hound.
dietNotes: Active hound needs high-quality protein diet. Clean ears regularly, especially after eating from deep bowls. Feed twice daily.

name: Black and Tan Coonhound
lore: Descended from Bloodhounds and Foxhounds, they were the first coonhound breed recognized by the AKC. Tireless trackers with a deep, resonant bay.
dietNotes: Active tracking dog needs calorie-dense food. Long, floppy ears need cleaning after meals. Feed twice daily to reduce bloat risk.

name: Walker Hound
lore: Developed from English Foxhounds by John W. Walker in Kentucky. Known for their speed, endurance, and ability to tree raccoons.
dietNotes: Athletic coonhound needs quality protein for endurance. Feed measured meals twice daily; working dogs may need increased portions.

name: English Foxhound
lore: One of the rarest AKC breeds in America despite centuries of English fox hunting heritage. Bred for stamina and pack cooperation.
dietNotes: Bred for pack life and endurance; needs high-protein, calorie-dense food. Active hunters need significantly more calories than pet dogs.

name: Redbone Coonhound
lore: An all-American breed with a stunning solid red coat. Featured in the beloved novel 'Where the Red Fern Grows' as loyal hunting companions.
dietNotes: Active hound breed needs balanced, protein-rich food. Prone to overeating; measure all meals. Keep ears clean after feeding.

name: Italian Greyhound
lore: A miniature Greyhound adored by Renaissance nobility. Frederick the Great of Prussia loved them so much he asked to be buried beside his.
dietNotes: Delicate toy breed with fast metabolism. Feed small, frequent meals of nutrient-dense food. Dental health requires regular attention.

name: Ibizan Hound
lore: Resembles the ancient Egyptian god Anubis. Brought to the Balearic island of Ibiza by Phoenician traders over 3,000 years ago.
dietNotes: Lean sighthound needs quality protein without excess fat. Naturally thin; visible ribs may be normal. Feed twice daily.

name: Norwegian Elkhound
lore: Vikings sailed with these fearless dogs over a thousand years ago. Bred to track and hold moose at bay until the hunter arrived.
dietNotes: Hardy Nordic breed prone to weight gain. Feed measured meals of quality food; reduce portions if activity decreases. Monitor kidney health.

name: Scottish Deerhound
lore: The Royal Dog of Scotland, once so prized that no one below the rank of Earl could own one. Sir Walter Scott called them the most perfect creature.
dietNotes: Giant sighthound prone to bloat. Feed 2-3 small meals daily. They are naturally lean; do not overfeed to 'fill them out.'

name: American Staffordshire Terrier
lore: Petey from 'The Little Rascals' was an AmStaff. Sergeant Stubby, the most decorated war dog of WWI, was also this breed.
dietNotes: Muscular breed needs high-protein diet. Active dogs with strong jaws; durable chew toys complement their feeding routine.

name: Border Terrier
lore: Bred on the Anglo-Scottish border to hunt foxes. Their otter-shaped head and wiry coat let them squeeze through tight spaces underground.
dietNotes: Active small terrier needs quality protein. Not typically food-obsessed but will eat well after exercise. Measured meals twice daily.

name: Kerry Blue Terrier
lore: Born black, their coat gradually turns a distinctive blue-gray by age two. Ireland's national terrier, used as an all-purpose farm dog.
dietNotes: Active terrier needs balanced protein-rich diet. Their non-shedding coat benefits from omega fatty acids and quality nutrition.

name: Irish Terrier
lore: Known as the 'Daredevil' of the terrier world. Served as messenger dogs in WWI trenches and were praised for incredible bravery under fire.
dietNotes: Active terrier needs quality protein diet. Prone to urinary stones; ensure adequate water intake and avoid high-purine foods.

name: Norfolk Terrier
lore: The smallest of the working terriers with drop ears. Cambridge University students kept them as ratters in their dorms in the 1880s.
dietNotes: Small terrier with a good appetite. Feed nutrient-dense small-breed food in measured portions. Dental care is important.

name: Norwich Terrier
lore: Nearly identical to the Norfolk Terrier except for their pricked ears. One of the smallest terrier breeds but fearless with vermin.
dietNotes: Small terrier with big appetite. Feed measured portions of quality small-breed food. Can be prone to weight gain if free-fed.

name: Wire Fox Terrier
lore: Has won more Best in Show titles at Westminster than any other breed. Asta from 'The Thin Man' films made them Hollywood stars.
dietNotes: Active terrier needs quality protein. Their wiry coat benefits from good nutrition with omega fatty acids. Feed twice daily.

name: Lakeland Terrier
lore: Bred in England's Lake District to protect lambs from foxes. Their narrow, flexible body could follow foxes deep into rocky dens.
dietNotes: Active small terrier needs high-quality food. Not typically food-driven but will benefit from consistent feeding schedule twice daily.

name: Sealyham Terrier
lore: Once the most popular terrier in Britain, now critically endangered. Alfred Hitchcock owned several and they appeared in his films.
dietNotes: Moderate activity breed; watch for weight gain. Feed quality food in measured portions. Their white coat benefits from good nutrition.

name: Cairn Terrier
lore: Toto from 'The Wizard of Oz' was a Cairn Terrier named Terry. Originally bred to hunt between cairns (stone piles) in the Scottish Highlands.
dietNotes: Hardy terrier with good appetite. Feed quality food in controlled portions. Prone to weight gain if overfed or under-exercised.

name: Australian Terrier
lore: The first breed developed in Australia, created to hunt snakes and rodents in the harsh outback. Tough and spirited despite their small size.
dietNotes: Small but hardy terrier needs quality, nutrient-dense food. Prone to diabetes; maintain consistent feeding schedule and healthy weight.

name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier
lore: The only breed named after a fictional character — from Sir Walter Scott's novel 'Guy Mannering.' Their topknot of silky hair is unique among terriers.
dietNotes: Long-backed breed; weight management protects the spine. Feed measured portions and avoid excess treats that lead to weight gain.

name: Boston Terrier
lore: The 'American Gentleman' thanks to their tuxedo-like markings. One of the first breeds developed in the USA, originating in Boston around 1870.
dietNotes: Flat-faced breed; use wide, shallow bowls. Prone to gas and digestive sensitivity; quality food with easily digestible ingredients helps.

name: Giant Schnauzer
lore: Originally drove cattle in the Bavarian Alps, later served as police and military dogs. The largest of the three Schnauzer breeds.
dietNotes: Large, active working dog needs high-protein, calorie-dense food. Feed twice daily to reduce bloat risk. Joint supplements are beneficial.

name: Standard Schnauzer
lore: The original Schnauzer, from which the Miniature and Giant were bred. Albrecht Durer painted them in the 15th century. Versatile farm guardians.
dietNotes: Active medium breed needs balanced nutrition. Not typically food-driven; consistent meals with quality protein twice daily.

name: Scottish Terrier
lore: Two US Presidents kept Scotties in the White House — FDR's Fala and George W. Bush's Barney. The Scottie dog is an iconic Monopoly game piece.
dietNotes: Moderate exercise breed; avoid overfeeding. Quality protein with measured portions. Prone to bladder cancer; consider cancer-preventive nutrition.

name: Tibetan Terrier
lore: Not actually a terrier — Tibetan monks bred them as 'Holy Dogs' and good luck charms. Their flat, snowshoe-like feet helped traverse Himalayan snow.
dietNotes: Long-lived breed benefits from a balanced diet with antioxidants. Their heavy coat needs nutritional support from omega fatty acids.

name: Silky Terrier
lore: Developed in Australia by crossing Yorkshire Terriers with Australian Terriers. Their glossy blue-and-tan coat is truly silky to the touch.
dietNotes: Small breed with beautiful silky coat. Nutrient-dense food with omega fatty acids supports coat health. Feed small portions twice daily.

name: Soft-Coated Wheaten Terrier
lore: Known as the 'Poor Man's Wolfhound' in Ireland. Born dark, their soft, wheat-colored coat develops over the first two years of life.
dietNotes: Prone to protein-wasting diseases; high-quality, easily digestible protein is essential. Avoid high-fat diets. Regular vet monitoring recommended.

name: Lhasa Apso
lore: Sentinel dogs of Tibetan monasteries for over a thousand years. The Dalai Lama traditionally gave them as gifts to honored visitors.
dietNotes: Small breed needs quality food. Their long coat requires nutritional support; omega fatty acids help maintain coat quality.

name: Flat-Coated Retriever
lore: Known as the 'Peter Pan' of dogs because they never seem to grow up. Once the most popular retriever in Britain before Labs and Goldens took over.
dietNotes: Very active sporting dog needs high-calorie, protein-rich food. Sadly cancer-prone breed; antioxidant-rich diet may help.

name: Curly-Coated Retriever
lore: The oldest of all retriever breeds, dating back to the late 1700s. Their tight, waterproof curls protect them in icy waters.
dietNotes: Active sporting breed needs balanced, protein-rich food. Their unique curly coat is low maintenance but benefits from good nutrition.

name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
lore: Maryland's state dog, bred to retrieve ducks from the icy Chesapeake Bay. Their oily, wavy coat repels water like a duck's feathers.
dietNotes: Hardy water retriever needs protein-rich diet with healthy fats. Their oily coat benefits from omega fatty acids in their food.

name: German Shorthaired Pointer
lore: The ultimate versatile hunting dog — they point, retrieve, and track on land and water. One of the most popular sporting breeds in the world.
dietNotes: Extremely active sporting dog needs high-calorie food. Working dogs may need 50% more calories than sedentary pets. Feed twice daily.

name: English Setter
lore: One of the oldest gundog breeds, known for their elegant, speckled 'belton' coat pattern. Gentle and sweet-natured, the aristocrat of setters.
dietNotes: Active sporting breed needs balanced nutrition with quality protein. Their feathered coat benefits from omega fatty acids.

name: Gordon Setter
lore: The heaviest of the setter breeds, developed by the Duke of Gordon in Scotland. Their striking black-and-tan coat is unmistakable in the field.
dietNotes: Large sporting breed needs protein-rich food. Deep-chested and prone to bloat; feed 2 meals daily and avoid exercise around mealtimes.

name: Brittany
lore: Originally called the Brittany Spaniel, they work more like pointers than spaniels. The most popular pointing breed for American bird hunters.
dietNotes: Extremely energetic sporting breed needs calorie-dense, high-protein food. Active hunting dogs may need significantly increased portions.

name: Clumber Spaniel
lore: The heaviest of all spaniels. British royals including Prince Albert and King Edward VII kept them. Named after Clumber Park in Nottinghamshire.
dietNotes: Heaviest spaniel breed; prone to weight gain. Strict portion control needed. Quality food with moderate calories to maintain healthy weight.

name: Welsh Springer Spaniel
lore: An ancient breed depicted in Welsh art from the Renaissance era. Their rich red-and-white coat makes them one of the most striking spaniels.
dietNotes: Active sporting breed needs balanced, protein-rich diet. Moderate eaters; feed quality food twice daily with appropriate portions.

name: Sussex Spaniel
lore: One of the rarest spaniel breeds, nearly extinct after WWII. Unique among spaniels for their distinctive rich golden-liver coat and low-slung build.
dietNotes: Low-slung breed prone to weight gain. Feed measured portions of quality food. Long back means excess weight risks disc problems.

name: Irish Water Spaniel
lore: The tallest of all spaniels with a distinctive 'rat tail' and tight liver-colored curls. One of the oldest and rarest spaniel breeds.
dietNotes: Active water dog needs protein-rich diet. Their unique curly coat benefits from omega fatty acids. Feed measured meals twice daily.

name: Kuvasz
lore: Ancient Hungarian flock guardian prized by King Matthias Corvinus, who trusted them more than his own guards. Nearly went extinct during WWII.
dietNotes: Large guardian breed needs controlled calories with joint-supporting nutrients. Feed 2-3 meals daily to prevent bloat.

name: Schipperke
lore: Little black foxlike dogs that guarded Belgian canal boats. Their name means 'little captain' in Flemish. Naturally tailless with a mischievous spirit.
dietNotes: Active small breed needs nutrient-dense food. Not prone to overeating but should have measured portions for optimal weight.

name: Belgian Sheepdog
lore: Also called the Groenendael, this elegant all-black Belgian shepherd served as message carriers and ambulance dogs in both World Wars.
dietNotes: Active herding breed needs high-protein food. Their dense black coat benefits from omega fatty acids. Adjust calories to activity level.

name: Briard
lore: Napoleon and Lafayette both owned Briards. This ancient French sheepdog served as sentries and supply carriers in the trenches of WWI.
dietNotes: Large herding breed needs protein-rich food. Deep chest means bloat risk; feed 2 meals daily. Extensive coat needs nutritional support.

name: Australian Kelpie
lore: Legendary Australian herding dogs that can manage thousands of sheep. Famous for running across the backs of sheep in packed yards.
dietNotes: Extremely active herding dog needs high-calorie, protein-dense food. Working dogs may need double the calories of pet dogs.

name: Old English Sheepdog
lore: Their shaggy coat once served as shearing material for their owners. The Dulux paint mascot made them one of the most recognizable breeds.
dietNotes: Large breed with enormous coat that hides weight gain. Weigh regularly and feed measured meals. Coat needs nutritional support.

name: Collie
lore: Lassie made them the most famous dog in the world. Queen Victoria fell in love with them at Balmoral and popularized the breed.
dietNotes: MDR1 gene means drug sensitivity; some foods interact. Quality protein with omega fatty acids for their luxurious coat.

name: Bouvier des Flandres
lore: Belgian cattle herders nearly wiped out in WWI. Lucky, a Bouvier, was the beloved dog of President Ronald Reagan. Powerful and versatile farm dogs.
dietNotes: Large working breed needs protein-rich food. Prone to bloat; feed 2-3 smaller meals. Bearded face collects food; wipe after eating.

name: Miniature Pinscher
lore: The 'King of Toys' predates the Doberman despite their similar look. Known for their distinctive hackney-like high-stepping gait.
dietNotes: Tiny breed with high metabolism. Feed nutrient-dense, small-breed food in measured portions. Prone to obesity if over-treated.

name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
lore: The oldest and largest of the four Swiss mountain dog breeds. Pulled heavy carts for Swiss dairymen and butchers through Alpine villages.
dietNotes: Giant breed needs large-breed formula with controlled growth nutrients. Very prone to bloat; feed 2-3 small meals daily.

name: Appenzeller Sennenhund
lore: One of four Swiss mountain dog breeds, the Appenzeller is the most energetic. Traditionally used to herd cattle and pull carts in the Swiss Alps.
dietNotes: Very active mountain breed needs high-calorie food. Working dogs require increased portions. Balanced diet supports their active lifestyle.

name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog
lore: The smallest of the four Swiss mountain dog breeds. A lively, self-confident herder from the Entlebuch valley near Lucerne.
dietNotes: Active herding breed needs balanced, protein-rich food. Feed measured meals twice daily; adjust portions to activity level.

name: Bullmastiff
lore: The 'Gamekeeper's Night Dog' — bred to catch poachers on English estates. They would pin intruders without biting, holding them until help arrived.
dietNotes: Giant breed prone to bloat; feed 2-3 small meals daily. Large-breed formula with joint support. Avoid exercise around mealtimes.

name: American Eskimo Dog
lore: Despite the name, they are of German Spitz origin. Became famous performing tricks in traveling circuses across 19th-century America.
dietNotes: Active Spitz breed needs quality protein. Their thick white coat benefits from omega fatty acids. Feed measured meals twice daily.

name: Affenpinscher
lore: The 'Monkey Dog' — their name means 'monkey-like terrier' in German. Originally bred to hunt rats in German kitchens and stables.
dietNotes: Tiny breed needs small, frequent meals of nutrient-dense food. Their flat face may benefit from small kibble or wet food.

name: Great Pyrenees
lore: Royal Dog of France under Louis XIV. These majestic white guardians have protected sheep from wolves and bears in the Pyrenees mountains for centuries.
dietNotes: Giant guardian breed; surprisingly modest appetite for their size. Feed large-breed formula in 2 meals daily. Prone to bloat.

name: Chow Chow
lore: One of the oldest breeds with a distinctive blue-black tongue. Ancient Chinese emperors kept hundreds as hunting dogs. Sigmund Freud had one at his sessions.
dietNotes: Prone to skin issues; quality protein with limited fillers helps. Their thick double coat needs nutritional support. Moderate portions.

name: Keeshond
lore: Named after Cornelis 'Kees' de Gyselaer, leader of Dutch Patriots. They were mascots of the Dutch political uprising against the House of Orange.
dietNotes: Spitz breed prone to weight gain under heavy coat. Regular weigh-ins important; feed measured portions of quality food.

name: Brussels Griffon
lore: Belgian stable dogs bred to catch rats. Queen Marie Henriette of Belgium popularized them as companion dogs. Their expressive face is almost human.
dietNotes: Tiny breed needs nutrient-dense food. Flat face can make eating messy; use wide, shallow bowls. Small frequent meals preferred.

name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi
lore: The older of the two Corgi breeds with a long fox-like tail. Welsh farmers used them to drive cattle by nipping at their heels for over 3,000 years.
dietNotes: Prone to obesity like their Pembroke cousins. Strict portion control essential. Long-backed; excess weight risks spinal problems.

name: Toy Poodle
lore: Bred down from Standard Poodles as companion dogs for Parisian aristocrats. Despite their dainty appearance, they are among the most intelligent breeds.
dietNotes: Tiny but long-lived breed needs nutrient-dense food. Small frequent meals to prevent hypoglycemia. Dental care is important.

name: Miniature Poodle
lore: The mid-sized Poodle, originally used for truffle hunting in France. Their hypoallergenic curly coat made them favorites in European royal courts.
dietNotes: Active small breed needs quality protein for energy and coat health. Hypoallergenic coat benefits from omega fatty acids.

name: Standard Poodle
lore: Originally a German water retriever — 'Pudel' means 'to splash.' The second most intelligent dog breed. Their iconic clip protected joints while swimming.
dietNotes: Active large breed needs protein-rich food. Prone to bloat; feed 2 meals daily. Curly coat needs nutritional support from quality fats.
